about: The words the page shows. Edit here and reload the browser; python -m gpuwm.gui.copy_lint checks them. {name} fields are filled in by the page.

app.name: ArWen
app.lost: The page lost touch with the server. It tries again every few seconds; forecasts keep running.
app.older_browser: This page needs a current browser. Edge, Chrome or Firefox all work.
app.map_failed: The map outlines did not load, so the map shows forecasts on a plain background.

shell.palette_placeholder: Search events, places, your forecasts and pages
shell.palette_enter: Enter to open, Esc to close
shell.open_assistant_sub: Ask about the wiki, a forecast or what fits this card
shell.assistant_off_line: Optional. Turn it on in Settings.

state_help.imported: Pictures only. This folder holds a render tree and no run record.
state_help.queued: Waiting to start. It starts by itself in its turn, once the card is free and its start is published.
state_help.ready: The plan is written and nothing has started.
state_help.stopped: The forecast was stopped. Everything it wrote is kept.
state_help.failed: The forecast stopped on an error. The reason is on its Results page.
state_help.stale: No end was recorded and no process is alive. The computer may have restarted.
state_help.unreadable: This folder's run records could not be read. The reason is in the page server's log.

runs.title: My forecasts
runs.data: {count} in the forecasts folder, newest first
runs.data_queued: {count} in the forecasts folder, {queued} of them queued
runs.cut: The newest {shown} of {total} in the forecasts folder. Older ones are not listed here; their folders are untouched.
runs.new_line: Place a box on the map, pick a start time and a grid, then start.
runs.updates_stopped: Updates from the machine stopped. Open it to resume them.
runs.folder_note: Forecasts started from a terminal show here too.
runs.from_wiki: Pick an event from the wiki
runs.queue_line: These start by themselves in this order, one at a time, when the card is free and their start is published.

create.title: New forecast
create.where_line: Click the map to place the box. Drag the box to move it, drag a corner to size it. Scroll to zoom.
create.no_box: No box yet. Click the map.
create.when_line: Any date from 1940 on. Pick a day on the calendar or type it, then the hour. The list under it says which data holds that start.
create.fine_line: Finer grids show storms in more detail and need more card memory. Each choice is checked against your card.

grids.name: Storms
grids.why: Thunderstorms show as storms. The usual choice.

grids.name: Fine
grids.why: Small features. Needs a small box or a big card.

create.levels_line: More levels split the same column more finely, from the ground to the same model top, and need more card memory and time. Each choice is priced by the engine for the grid above.

levels.name: More
levels.why: Finer near the ground and through the storm.

levels.name: Many
levels.why: Finer steps all the way up.

levels.name: Most
levels.why: The finest ladder offered here. Slowest.

create.too_big_levels: Too big: needs {need} of {budget} GB usable. Pick fewer levels, a coarser grid or a smaller box.
create.levels_other_hint: A whole number of levels. The engine says if it cannot use it.
create.card_line_usable: Checked for a {card} card ({budget} GiB usable).
create.too_big: Too big: needs {need} of {budget} GiB usable. Make the box smaller.
create.review_line: Dashed on the map: the box you asked for. Solid: the grid the engine fitted.
create.name: Name
create.name_hint: Letters, digits, dots, dashes. It becomes the folder name.
create.card_hint: The run is sized to fit this.
create.section_hint: For an xsec: product, enter each end as latitude,longitude,latitude,longitude. The ends must be at least 1 km apart.
create.fit_waiting: Asking the engine for the fit.
create.queued: Queued in place {place}. It starts by itself when the card is free.
create.queued_data: Queued in place {place}. It starts by itself once its start is published and the card is free.
create.start_now_off: The card is held, so a second forecast cannot start beside it. Queue it and it starts when the card is free.
create.start_now_off_short: The card is busy, so this forecast has to wait.
create.start_off_data: {why} Queue it and it starts once a check confirms the start.
create.start_off_data_short: The start is not confirmed yet, so it waits.
create.starts_for_data: Once a check confirms the start is published.
create.need_box: Place the box on the map first.
create.where_find: Or find a past event above: its box, date and length fill in.
create.find_placeholder: A storm, a place or a year
create.find_none: No event in the wiki matches. Try a place, a year or a kind of storm.
create.date_future: That date has not happened yet.
create.checking_date: Checking which data holds this start...
create.start_queue_only: This start is not confirmed published yet. You can go on: Queue it holds the forecast and starts it once a check confirms the start.
create.sources_wait: Reading the list of data sources. The calendar works now.
create.kind_reanalysis: Reanalysis: the best estimate of what the weather was.
create.kind_analysis: Analysis: the forecast system's own estimate of the weather at each run's start.
create.kind_regional: Regional forecast model: the box has to sit inside its area.
create.switched: {from} does not hold this start, so {to} is picked. {why}
create.none_has: No data source holds this start. Pick another date or hour.
create.maybe_line: These may hold this start. Each row says why it is not sure.
create.start_hour_hint: 0 starts from the cycle itself; 30 starts from its 30 hour forecast.
create.whole_cycle_hint: Off, the forecast starts once its first hours are posted and waits whenever it reaches an hour the source has not posted yet. On, it starts once the last hour is posted.
create.posting_checking: Asking the engine when this data is posted.
create.posting_failed: The posting schedule could not be read ({why}). The run's own check decides when it starts.
create.posting_engine_whole: Starts once the whole cycle is posted.
create.posting_engine_whole_default: Starts once the whole cycle is posted: this engine does not start a forecast before the cycle's last hour.
create.posting_refused: The engine says this start can never run.
create.posting_whole: Starts once the whole cycle is posted, about {final}.
create.posting_cycle: This source posts each cycle whole ({why}), so it starts once the cycle is posted, about {final}.
create.posting_unprobeable: This source cannot be asked before its files arrive; the run starts once they are in, about {final}.
create.posting_ready: Its first hours are posted, so it starts now.
create.posting_waiting: Starts once its first hours are posted, about {ready}.
create.posting_rest: The last hour is due about {final}; the forecast waits at any hour not posted yet.
create.posting_late: An hour more than {late} min late stops it, keeping every frame written.
create.posting_unknown_time: a time the schedule does not give
create.cycle_lead: the {cycle} run, from its forecast hour {hour}
create.draft_reset: This link holds only the box, date and source, so the other choices start again from their defaults here at Where.
create.layout_following: The event's finer nest follows the storm inside this {dx} grid, set up the way the event page runs it.
create.layout_following_dropped: This choice drops the storm-following nest of the event. It stays only with the {dx} grid, the event's box, the engine's own levels and physics, and no nest ladder.
create.layout_nests: The event's nests stay inside this {dx} grid.
create.layout_nests_dropped: This choice drops the event's nests. They stay only with the {dx} grid and no nest ladder.
create.ladder_hint: Finer nests inside the outer grid. Leave it on none to use the grid chosen above.
create.ladder_auto: The deepest that fits the card
create.clock_hint: Adaptive follows the flow and runs faster where the grid allows it. The engine picks adaptive where it is covered.
create.physics_line: Each table is one part of the model. The default set for this grid runs unless you pick another row. Every pick is checked by the engine at this grid, place and time.
create.physics_checking: The engine is checking this set.
create.physics_default_set: The default set for this grid runs. Pick a row to change one part.
create.physics_lands: Goes into the plan as the set
create.physics_mix_lands: No named set matches these schemes, so they go into the plan as they are, and the engine writes them into this forecast's experiment.
create.physics_cost_reference: The Cost column is measured against the data source's own default set, not the default for this grid:
create.from_assistant: Filled in by the assistant. Change anything before you start.

mapviewer.picture_help: The renderer's own picture, title and colour bar included
mapviewer.no_pictures: No maps yet. They appear here as the renderer draws them.
mapviewer.no_selected_picture: The grids turned on have no picture at this time. Pick another time, or turn on a grid that has one.
mapviewer.no_grid_on: Every grid is turned off. Turn one on to see its map.
mapviewer.no_basemap: These maps have no coastlines, borders or state lines: this install is missing its map files. Reinstall the gpuwm-data package to bring them back.
mapviewer.not_placed: {grids}: the renderer kept no position for this picture, so it is not on the map.
mapviewer.no_grid: The grid of this run is not on record yet, so its maps cover the renderer's whole frame.
mapviewer.stop_confirm: Stop this forecast? Everything it has written is kept.
mapviewer.stopped: Stop sent. The forecast keeps what it wrote.
mapviewer.ready_intro: This forecast is ready and has not started.
mapviewer.failed: The forecast stopped on an error.
mapviewer.stale: No end was recorded and nothing is running. The computer may have restarted.
mapviewer.follow_lost: Updates from the machine stopped. The state and pictures shown are the last ones received.
mapviewer.resumed: Following the machine again. Its latest state and pictures appear here.
mapviewer.pace: {grids}, {speed} real time, the {pace} grid sets the pace
mapviewer.downscale_help: Run a finer forecast inside this one, driven by its saved output

downscale.title: Finer forecast inside this one
downscale.place_note: Click the map for the finer forecast's centre, or draw its box.
downscale.drawing: Drag a box on the map.
downscale.centre: Centre {place}. The engine sizes it to the card.
downscale.need_place: Click the map for the finer forecast's centre, or draw its box.
downscale.edges: Its edges are driven by this grid's saved frames, one every {minutes} minutes.
downscale.name: Name
downscale.reviewing: The engine is planning the finer forecast. This reads the saved frames and measures the card.
downscale.start_note: This is the grid Start runs. It is drawn on the map.
downscale.changed: The form changed since the review. Review again before Start.

results.title: Results
results.failed: The forecast stopped on an error.

explore.title: Files
explore.intro: The pictures of a forecast, by domain, picture and day, exactly as the renderer wrote them.
explore.tree: Pictures, as the renderer filed them

wait.about: What a forecast waiting at a seam says in its live line: a source hour not posted yet, or a boundary interval not prepared yet.
wait.preparation: waiting for boundary interval {interval} to be prepared

preparation.about: The live line while a forecast prepares, from the engine's own records: steps by the engine's key, runtime phases by name.

steps.child_initialize: Start state for the inner grids
steps.hierarchy_static: Checking the inner grids' static fields

phases.resolve-terrain-clock: Reading the terrain for the time step
phases.prepare-case: Reading the starting data and building the start state

machines.title: Machines
machines.line: The computers that run and draw forecasts: this one, any computer you reach by SSH, and cloud machines. Adding one is one row; nothing is installed until you press Install.
machines.add_title: Add a computer by its SSH host
machines.add_line: It is checked over SSH before it is saved: its card, its free memory and the gpuwm version there. Key sign-in only; a password is never asked for or kept.
machines.name: Name
machines.host_hint: user@host, or a Host name from your SSH config
machines.workspace_hint: The one folder ArWen writes in there
machines.geog_hint: Optional: where that machine keeps the static geography
machines.removed: Removed {name}. Nothing on the machine was touched.
machines.install_line: This computer's gpuwm wheel for Linux and its gpuwm_data wheel are copied to the machine and installed in its own folder.
machines.install_folder_hint: The folder that holds both wheels of this version
machines.install_from_hint: This computer, or another machine in the list
machines.install_starting: Copying the wheels and starting the install.
machines.install_need_folder: Name the folder that holds the wheels.
machines.draw_title: Draw a forecast on a machine
machines.draw_line: Any forecast, running or finished, can be drawn on any machine here. The pictures come back into the forecast's folder as they are drawn.
machines.drawing: Drawing on {machine}. The pictures appear on the forecast's map as they are written.
machines.no_runs: There is no forecast to draw yet.
machines.empty: Only this computer so far. Add a computer you reach by SSH to run or draw forecasts there.

settings.title: Settings
settings.assistant_line: The assistant is optional and off until you turn it on. Off, nothing is downloaded, no model server runs and no card memory is used.
settings.uses_server: It uses the model server at
settings.downloaded: Its model is on this computer. It loads onto the card when you ask something and leaves while a forecast runs.
settings.models_title: Models it downloads for each card
settings.models_line: The largest row your card reaches is the one it uses. Each file is pinned to its published revision and checked against its published SHA-256.
settings.brought_line: Strong models the assistant does not download. Run one in LM Studio, Ollama, llama.cpp or the build its row names, and give its address in the assistant's settings; its licence is yours to accept.
